newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia criticises Israel, urges Mideast dialogue.
newsitem.headline: Russia criticises Israel, urges Mideast dialogue.

text.p: Russia, expressing concern about tensions in the Middle East, castigated Israel on Thursday over clashes in the West Bank and defended the role of Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat.

"We are seriously concerned about clashes between the Palestinian population and Israeli security forces in the West Bank," said foreign ministry spokesman Gennady Tarasov, whose country is a co-sponsor of the Middle East peace process.
"The deterioration of the situation has been caused by Israel's actions to unilaterally change the status quo in East Jerusalem," he told a news briefing.
Tarasov was referring to Israel's building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem which has provoked protests by Palestinians and more than a week of clashes.

A Palestinian suicide bomber blew himself up at a Tel Aviv cafe last Friday, killing three Israeli women. Israel said the Palestinian Authority led by Arafat gave the green light for the attack, but later said it had no evidence to back this up.
Tarasov said Arafat should not be blamed.
"The Palestinian leadership is no less interested in stopping extremism and violence than the Israeli authorities," he said.
"So, there are no grounds for the accusations aimed at Arafat alleging that he almost gave the green light to terrorists whose action in Tel Aviv we resolutely condemned."
Moscow has been trying to reassert itself in the Middle East ater long playing second fiddle to the United States. Tarasov said the way forward in the region was through dialogue.
"Both countries must make energetic efforts to prevent confrontation and to normalise the situation," he said.
"Confrontation rhetoric which brings grist to the mill of the opponents of peace and harmony in the region must, we are convinced, give way to responsible dialogue."
